text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former Cabinet Minister Elijah Mwangale and the Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Lands and Settlements Josiah Sang are named in parliament in a land scandal in which Sang asked the Treasury to release a 300 million shillings government loan to pay for a farm earlier valued at 16 million shillings.
- Nairobi Stock Exchange Chairman Jimnah Mbaru says trading in corporate bonds has been approved by the Capital Markets Authority and will soon be listed and traded at the Nairobi bourse.
- The Kenya Power and Lighting Company says it still hopes to renegotiate tariffs with Uganda for power supplied from the Owen Falls Dam in Uganda.

- In a mini-cabinet reshuffle, President Daniel arap Moi sacks top Cabinet Minister John Sambu and appoints former Executive Chairman of the defunct Kenya National Assurance Corporation Henry Kosgey as the new Environment and Natural Resources Minister.
- Giant milk chain Kenya Cooperative Creameries chairman Stanley Metto accuses Nairobi City Council's public health department of being used by politicians to sabotage the cooperative.

- The Law Society of Kenya declares null a controversial circular issued by Chief Justice Cockar directing magistrates not to grant bail to suspects facing more than one criminal case of similar nature.

- Cabinet Minister Simeon Nyachae dismisses his political detractors as "shallow-minded" and emphasises he is proud of his performance in his Agriculture, Livestock Development and Marketing portfolio.
